# Tcl execution evidence

## Question

> A failed numeric conversion must not silently select a default read count, seek offset, wrapping length or debug Boolean. Public workers may use different release-specific converters and option grammars, and an unavailable worker cannot establish conversion behaviour. Cursor changes, debug state queries and errorCode updates distinguish actual command effects from conversion errors.

> For the exact invalid, negative, zero, positive and oversized operands, what public read/seek/base64 maxlen/debug results, errorCode values and cursor or debug-state effects occur on each measured C Tcl release and Jim build?

## Assumptions

Assumptions were not separately recorded in the retained capture.

Recorded scope and limits:

> One unchanged ASCII probe with physical LF creates a distinct owned per-provider disposable file whose runtime bytes are abcdef followed by LF. Public operations are read(channel,count), seek(channel,offset[,origin]), binary encode base64 -maxlen and interp debug child -frame. Each case seeds errorCode as R2286 SEEDED, records catch result/errorCode as hexadecimal, and reads tell(channel) where applicable. Debug BEFORE/AFTER 0 are supplied constants, not measurements; the separate debug-frame-state query measures debug state. Five C processes supply 43 rows each and Jim supplies 32 rows, totalling 247 rows, with process exit0 and empty stderr. The retained cases.json is a request-only declaration; actual receipts and streams supply results. Version comes from the independently captured same-ELF 627 VERSION stream. Original implementation C/Jim source, internal conversion/cleanup chronology, callbacks, Native operands, full build/load closure, current Rust outcomes and F5/TMM are unmeasured.

## Script

```tcl-visible
# Exact ASCII source, Tcl 8.4-compatible except the public workers being measured.
# R2286_IO_PROBE_FILE selects an owned per-provider disposable file.
if {![info exists ::env(R2286_IO_PROBE_FILE)]} {error "owned probe file is required"}
proc hx {value} {binary scan $value H* encoded; return $encoded}
proc report {label script before channel} {
    set ::errorCode {R2286 SEEDED}
    set code [catch {uplevel 1 $script} result]
    set errorCode $::errorCode
    set after $before
    if {$channel ne ""} {set after [tell $channel]}
    puts [list CASE $label CODE $code RESULT_HEX [hx $result] ERRORCODE_HEX [hx $errorCode] BEFORE $before AFTER $after]
}
set path $::env(R2286_IO_PROBE_FILE)
set writer [open $path w]
puts -nonewline $writer "abcdef\n"
close $writer
foreach count {bad 1.5 -1 0 2 18446744073709551616} {
    set channel [open $path r]
    seek $channel 3
    report [list read $count] [list read $channel $count] 3 $channel
    close $channel
}
foreach offset {bad 1.5 -1 0 2 18446744073709551616} {
    foreach origin {omitted start current} {
        set channel [open $path r]
        seek $channel 3
        if {$origin eq "omitted"} {set script [list seek $channel $offset]} else {set script [list seek $channel $offset $origin]}
        report [list seek $offset $origin] $script 3 $channel
        close $channel
    }
}
set channel [open $path r]
seek $channel 3
report {seek bad invalid-origin} [list seek $channel bad invalid-origin] 3 $channel
close $channel
foreach length {bad 1.5 -1 0 2 18446744073709551616} {
    report [list binary-base64-maxlen $length] [list binary encode base64 -maxlen $length abcdef] NA ""
}
foreach flag {bad 1.5 false true 0 1} {
    set child r2286_io_debug
    if {[catch {interp create $child} createResult]} {
        puts [list CASE debug-create CODE 1 RESULT_HEX [hx $createResult]]
        break
    }
    report [list debug-frame $flag] [list interp debug $child -frame $flag] 0 ""
    report [list debug-frame-state $flag] [list interp debug $child -frame] NA ""
    interp delete $child
}
file delete $path
```
